title: Name playbook apply routes in the context map
body:
## Summary
The Playbooks context map omits the apply and apply-batch routes and still points at PlaybooksPanel.tsx, which is not in the tree.

## Description
context-map.json lists apiRoutes /api/org/playbooks, /api/org/playbooks/[id], and /api/org/playbooks/[id]/repos. filePaths already include apply/route.ts and apply-batch/route.ts. The description's entry point is src/components/org/PlaybooksPanel.tsx; no such file exists. Editing the context map is an architecture change for this sweep.

## Flow
- Read the Playbooks filePaths and apiRoutes in context-map.json
- Compare them to the route files on disk
- Search the tree for PlaybooksPanel.tsx

## Expected impact
Agents and the coverage picker would see the rollout routes as part of the context. A wrong edit to the map would mis-route later sweeps.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the map matches the routes that exist
Before: 2 of 5 playbook routes missing from apiRoutes, and 1 named entry point absent on disk
After: not measured; the map was not edited
Method: probe - counted routes on disk against the apiRoutes array
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: context-map.json apiRoutes at the Playbooks entry; filePaths include apply and apply-batch; no PlaybooksPanel.tsx in src/

title: Show which playbook version a repo adopted
body:
## Summary
appliedVersion is written when a playbook is stamped and has no production reader.

## Description
applyPlaybook and stampLandedPlaybook store appliedVersion. A repo-wide search finds those writers and one test. The card shows PlaybookRow.version when it is greater than 1, and that card is outside this context's filePaths.

## Flow
- Grep appliedVersion across src
- Confirm the only non-test hits are the two writers
- Leave the card unread because it is not in the round's paths

## Expected impact
An operator could see that a repo is still on an older playbook version. The UI change belongs to the practices surface.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a stamped version is visible
Before: 0 production readers of appliedVersion
After: not measured; the card was not edited
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/db/playbooks.ts applyPlaybook upsert; src/lib/db/playbook-adoption.ts stampLandedPlaybook; src/lib/db/practice-adoption.playbook.test.ts asserts the write
note: out of scope (card not in Playbooks filePaths); --ab was not passed

title: Answer an unknown org on playbook list with 404
body:
## Summary
POST create now 404s an unknown org. GET list still returns 200 and an empty array.

## Description
listPlaybooks returns [] when getOrgId is null. The GET route returns that as { playbooks: [] }. On a deployment where open dashboards are enabled, canReadOrg is true for any slug, so a typo looks like an org with no standards. listPlaybooks is also called from PracticesTab and the briefing, which are outside this context.

## Flow
- Auth-off open dashboards, GET /api/org/playbooks?org=typo
- requireOrgRead allows the read
- listPlaybooks returns []
- Response is 200

## Expected impact
A typo'd slug would 404 instead of looking empty. Changing the null-versus-empty contract touches the practices tab and the briefing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - unknown org is not an empty library
Before: 1 of 1 unknown-org list reads on an open dashboard return 200 []
After: not measured
Method: simulation - walked the gate and listPlaybooks return
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/db/playbooks.ts listPlaybooks returns [] when orgId is null; src/app/api/org/playbooks/route.ts GET returns playbooks ?? []; src/lib/authz.ts canReadOrg falls through to openOrgDashboardsEnabled
note: out of scope callers: PracticesTab and briefing; --ab was not passed

title: Keep updatedAt still when a playbook is archived
body:
## Summary
An archive toggle that really changes the flag still moves updatedAt, which the row presents as the last content edit.

## Description
updatePlaybook now skips a write when nothing changed, so an identical patch no longer moves updatedAt. A real archive still calls prisma.playbook.update, and Playbook.updatedAt is @updatedAt, so the clock moves even though version does not. The schema is outside this context.

## Flow
- PATCH { archived: true } on a live playbook
- updatePlaybook writes archived and does not increment version
- Prisma bumps updatedAt

## Expected impact
The last-edit time would stay put on an archive. That needs a schema change, which this round did not make.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - archive is not a content edit
Before: 1 of 1 real archive toggles bump updatedAt
After: not measured
Method: probe - read the update path and the @updatedAt field
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/db/playbooks.ts updatePlaybook writes data.archived when the flag differs; prisma/schema.prisma Playbook.updatedAt is @updatedAt
note: schema is outside the Playbooks paths; --ab was not passed
